extraction_supporting_text.adjusted_model: In a sensitivity analysis we used logistic regression models to calculate ORs and 95% CIs of prostate cancer for rye- and oatmeal consumption in early life for incident cases only, adjusting for the same covariates as was done in the third model.
extraction_supporting_text.ci_level: In a sensitivity analysis we used logistic regression models to calculate ORs and 95% CIs of prostate cancer for rye- and oatmeal consumption in early life for incident cases only, adjusting for the same covariates as was done in the third model.
extraction_supporting_text.comparison_group: Men consuming oatmeal more than five times per week, had an OR of 0.80 (95% CI: 0.54-1.19) for total prostate cancer and 0.93 (95% CI: 0.40-2.19) for advanced disease compared with men with low oatmeal consumption (≤4 times/ week) in adolescence.
extraction_supporting_text.design: In a sensitivity analysis we used logistic regression models to calculate ORs and 95% CIs of prostate cancer for rye- and oatmeal consumption in early life for incident cases only, adjusting for the same covariates as was done in the third model.
extraction_supporting_text.population: Among the 347 prostate cancer cases who reported their dietary habits, 214 were diagnosed before and 133 after completing the FFQ.
extraction_supporting_text.reference_group: Men consuming oatmeal more than five times per week, had an OR of 0.80 (95% CI: 0.54-1.19) for total prostate cancer and 0.93 (95% CI: 0.40-2.19) for advanced disease compared with men with low oatmeal consumption (≤4 times/ week) in adolescence.
